candidate_facts.text: China entered the Korean War to support North Korea against United Nations forces led by the United States.
China feared that UN advances, particularly toward the Yalu River, would lead to encirclement or regime change in North Korea, prompting its intervention.
China warned the United States through neutral diplomats that it would intervene to protect its national security if US forces advanced too close to its border.
Mao Zedong argued that allowing the US to occupy all of Korea would weaken Asian communist revolutionary power.
Mao Zedong argued that allowing the US to occupy all of Korea would allow American influence to spread negatively across the Far East.
China's initial goal in the Korean War was not the conquest of South Korea but the preservation of North Korea as a buffer state.
